Nothing in the catalog entry or REFERENCES.md shows that this FC has two free PWM outputs on a timer that is not shared with the DShot motor outputs. Betaflight's servo_tilt is camera stabilisation, not a control output. Servo support in Betaflight is an optional cloud-build feature, and only some mixer types support it. fd.iwth and Mistral both run custom firmware. If the outputs or the firmware path don't exist, the drone cannot steer, and the brief explicitl
problems.fix: Pick the firmware and prove it. Record in the catalog, with a source: the FC's resource/timer map, which pads become the servo outputs (for example M3/M4 or LED on a separate timer), and the firmware. INAV's multirotor mixer with servo rules plus per-timer output mode is the usual path; if you use INAV, its equivalent of the 80 % cap is max_throttle. Write the exact CLI (mixer/smix or INAV mixer r

problems.issue: DESIGN.md step 2 presses both dowels in first, then step 3 fits horn_roll on the roll servo and step 4 'slides gimbal_outer's -X pad onto the roll dowel'. That cannot be done. To engage the 20 mm dowel the ring has to start about 11 mm toward +X and move -X, but then its +X lug overlaps horn_roll and the servo, which are already fitted. The pitch axis has the same problem: the hub's +Y lug would overlap horn_pitch. ASSEMBLY.md says 'press the dowel into ring_low' without saying when or from which side. The press holes are through holes, so a workable order exists, but it is not the one written
problems.fix: Rewrite the order. Fit the servo and horn, bolt the ring or hub to the horn while it is aligned with the pivot, and only then press the dowel in from outside: through ring_low's -X plate into gimbal_outer, and through gimbal_outer's -Y pad into the hub. Back up the yoke arm or pad in a vise while pressing. Add an assembly `insert` direction for the pins so the engine checks this.
problems.resolved_how: no part was redrawn; closed by the next review/check result

problems.issue: The XT60 is held by one cable tie plus a stop block that only resists pushing in. XT60 mating and unmating forces are tens of newtons. The connector's outer end sits at r 37.65, inside the 39 mm plate edge, so you can't hold the drone-side connector while you unplug. Every battery removal pulls the male XT60 outward through the tie, and the 14 AWG solder cups take the load.
problems.fix: Capture the connector in both directions. Use a printed U-cradle or pocket with a lip in front of the XT60 body's shoulder (or a second stop on the outer side plus a clamp strap), or move the connector out so its body protrudes past the plate edge and can be gripped. Strain-relieve the main lead to the plate with the tie.
problems.resolved_how: no part was redrawn; closed by the next review/check result

problems.issue: WIRING.md step 1 says to 'cut 2 x 100 mm AWG 12 and solder battery -> xt60', and the BOM buys 0.2 m of 12 AWG for it. Also, the pack's lead length (not in the catalog) has to reach the 97 mm minimum cut over the ring_top edge.

problems.issue: DESIGN.md, STATUS.md and the ring_low docstring say the bosses, webs and lug ribs touch the bed. They do not. In print orientation only the four 4 mm yoke-bridge webs (18 tall) reach z 0: STL bed contact is 1464 mm². The tube-boss ends float 4 mm up (14 tall) and the lug ribs 8 mm up (10 tall), and the 7222 mm² plate face is 18 mm up on supports. A 124 g, 111 mm tall part standing on four thin strips is acceptable on textured PEI with supports, but marginal, and the documentation is wrong.
problems.fix: Make the bed-contact features one height. Trim the bridge webs to 14 mm (flush with the bosses, then re-run yoke_fea) or raise the bosses to 18 mm (longer tube engagement). Do not raise the 30-degree rib to 18 mm: the ph_top/servo route point [26.8, 20, 100] passes about 4 mm from that rib's centre line at z 100. Correct the text.

problems.issue: Remaining s5 detail. ENGINEERING.md s5 says inside corners on any load path get r >= 1 mm and outside edges a 0.5-1 mm chamfer. It is a rule, not a margin-dependent option. The motor_hub fork, arm and lug roots carry all of the thrust, and the gimbal_outer pad-to-ring corners carry it too; neither has a fillet, and no part has bed-edge chamfers. The static FEA margins (>= 3.6x on top of SF 3; the hub and ring peaks sit at the dowel bore and servo pad, not the roots) make this low risk. That is why it stays minor, but it does not waive the rule on a part that sees motor vibration.
problems.fix: Add 1-1.5 mm fillets at the hub fork, arm and lug-to-disc vertical inside edges and at the gimbal_outer pad-to-ring inside corners (features.safe_fillet, same pattern as the ring_low disc corners), plus 0.5 mm bed-edge chamfers. Re-run gimbal_fea and outer_fea.
problems.resolved_how: no part was redrawn; closed by the next review/check result

problems.issue: Metadata/model_settings.config is missing objects. plate_1 has gimbal_outer but not leg_1 (its object tag is at byte 641575). plate_2 has leg_2, leg_3 and ring_low but not motor_hub (byte 1329357). plate_3 has ring_top but not ring_mid (byte 407916) or motor_plate (byte 1417221). Cause: `head = files[model][:200000]` in _write_part_settings only regex-scans the first 200 kB of the model XML, so any object after a large mesh is skipped. As a result motor_hub (all thrust, 3 M3 inserts; meant to be 50 % / 4 walls) and leg_1 (crash-loaded; 25 % / 4 walls) slice at the printer defaults (typically 1
problems.fix: Scan the whole model XML for object tags (drop the 200 kB cap, or stream it with iterparse and stop at <build>), or take the object ids from the mesher that writes the plate. Add a test with a multi-object plate whose second object starts past 200 kB, and assert that every object id gets an entry. Rebuild.

problems.issue: `kerf review-status tvc_drone` reports geometry 721479e716c80d8c, but out/report.json is 06bd0f2cab76ce9b; `kerf status` shows 'build PASS (stale)' and 'eval FAIL'. The current geometry has no check, renders or FEA.

problems.issue: The FEA uses a solid model and the print is 30 % infill with 4 perimeters. lug_fea is 7.88 vs 13 MPa. I accept 30 % + 4 walls without a modifier, given the SF 3 load case.

problems.issue: The teardropped servo-tab taps now use the horizontal pilot tap_h = 2.10 mm, which is larger than the M2 major diameter (2.0). The Bambu table's larger horizontal value makes up for the drooping top of a round horizontal hole. A teardrop already removes that droop, so applying both may leave the thread-forming tab screws with little bite. The ring lock taps (M3 PETG tap_h 2.78, for set screws) are fine.
problems.fix: Print a pin/tap coupon (`kerf calibrate`) with a teardropped M2 hole before the full parts. If the screws spin, set a negative tap calibration offset for the printer. Engine follow-up: decide whether tap_h should apply to teardrop holes or only to plain round horizontal ones.

problems.issue: First recorded here (the warning comes from the ENG-7..20 engine and was already in the 12:42 report): the 20 mm motion.pin_3mm is 1.5 mm / 1.0 mm shorter than the 21.5 / 21.0 mm span. The pin is a press fit in one side (DESIGN.md interface table), so it is retained, but the free-side bore is only partly filled.
problems.fix: Press each pin flush with the outer face of its press side so the whole shortfall sits at the press-side end and the free bearing bore is fully engaged. Optional: lengthen the span to a stocked length or add a note to DESIGN.md.

problems.issue: Carried over and documented in DESIGN.md assembly step 6: a straight 1.5 mm key cannot reach the two upper M2 horn screws.
problems.fix: Use a ball-end 1.5 mm key as the DESIGN says. List it in the tools section of the BOM if it isn't there already.
